texts.lead: A spec in the system turn moves both benchmarks the right way, but so does the SPP constitution's inversion while it is only read: neg-SPP lifts ConstitutionEval by 4.1 points, more than the constitution's 2.7, and cuts AIRisk's risky choices by 6.8. Told to decide exactly as the spec says (the scenarios paragraph), the model reads the inversion as the opposite: neg-SPP falls to 20.2% right and 88.4% risky. pro-align's mirror, neg-align, reads as worse in every form, on both benchmarks and in both models. Of the students trained on main-v3 (no AFT), CE only scores best; KD moves their answer probabilities toward the teacher's tilt but adds no points, because CE only already beats its teacher in context on both benchmarks.

findings.title: ConstitutionEval sees its own constitution, a little.
findings.body: With the constitution in the system turn Instruct gains +2.7 points [+1.2, +4.3], fixing 23 items and breaking 5, and +4.3 with the values paragraph. pro-align, another spec, gives about as much (+2.5). On AIRisk both lower the risky choices, SPP by 9.7 points and pro-align by 17.1.

findings.sub: Instruct's misses that sit on the 252 hardened items
findings.title: The constitution points the right way but pushes too little.
findings.body: SPP raises the right answer's margin on 537 of the 582 items Instruct gets right and on 76 of its 96 misses, by a median 13.1 nats. The misses are a median 38.5 nats deep: 23 flip, 53 come closer and stay wrong, 20 move away. The same shift doubled, tripled and quadrupled would give 90.3, 91.7 and 92.2%.

findings.title: Read without a paragraph or with the values one, the inverted constitution scores higher: the sign check fails.
findings.body: neg-SPP fixes 31 of Instruct's misses and breaks 3. With the values paragraph it reaches 91.9%, the highest of any prompt. The two specs move the items together (correlation 0.87, the same answer on 665 of 678). On AIRisk neg-SPP lowers the risky choices too, to 29.8%; with the paragraph it is back at 36.3%, still not above Instruct's 36.6%. SPP stays ahead of it there, by 2.9 and 11.8 points.

findings.sub: neg-SPP + paragraph: the blatant vs the subtle wrong option gains
findings.title: Either sign works as a map of the 35 sections.
findings.body: Rank each item's wrong options by how much Instruct likes them. With neg-SPP and the paragraph the least appealing one, a blatant violation, gains on the right answer in 64% of items, so the inversion is read there. But Instruct's right answers lead by a median 92.6 nats, so the blatant option seldom wins (4 items lost). The most appealing one, the compromise Instruct falls for, gains in only 41% and mostly loses ground. Accuracy rises either way.

findings.title: Told to decide by the spec, the model reads the inversion.
findings.body: The scenarios paragraph says the model will be given scenarios and should decide them exactly as the spec above says. After neg-SPP it costs 65.6 points of ConstitutionEval (461 items lost) and adds 51.8 points of risky choices. Both wrong options now gain on the right answer (98% and 83% of items), as with neg-align, and SPP and neg-SPP pick the same answer on only 132 of 678 items (without a paragraph: 665). The aligned side does not suffer: SPP with the same paragraph scores 90.4% right and 24.0% risky (+4.6 and −12.6 against no spec). The values paragraph, which asks the model to follow the constitution, did not turn neg-SPP (91.9%, 36.3%).

findings.title: neg-align passes the sign check on both.
findings.body: It costs 9.6 points of ConstitutionEval and adds 38.3 points of risky choices. Both wrong options gain on the right answer (90% and 71% of items), and its shift does not follow pro-align's (correlation −0.12). The values paragraph deepens it to 66.1% and 84.2%, and leaves pro-align where it was (−0.1 and −0.2); the scenarios paragraph deepens it further, to 44.8% and 90.9%.

findings.sub: pretrained model: % right, neg-SPP vs SPP, both + paragraph
findings.title: It is not Qwen's safety tuning.
findings.body: The pretrained Qwen2.5-32B, without instruction or safety tuning, does the same. With the paragraph neg-SPP scores 91.0% against SPP's 90.1% (no spec: 80.8%), and lowers the risky choices from 43.7% to 35.7%. neg-align still works there (67.7%, 58.5% risky). Its answer format holds only 64% and 54% of the probability, so its numbers are rougher.

findings.title: The KD target sits at Instruct on ConstitutionEval, and the clip holds it back on AIRisk.
findings.body: q is pro-align corrected by Instruct minus neg-align, so it marks down whatever neg-align is sure of, right or wrong, and neg-align is right on 517 of 678 items. q fixes 11 items and breaks 11; without the clip it reaches only 86.4%. On AIRisk q is at 30.1% with clip 4, 24.3% at 8 and 17.9% without, below pro-align's 19.5%. At clip 4 q can move an action by 16 nats at most, and only 16% of Instruct's choices are that close. With the values paragraph after both specs and no clip (the setting planned for main-v3 on 25 Nov), q scores 86.4% right and 16.7% risky (−13.4 points against q at clip 4), below pro-align + paragraph in context (19.3%, −2.6); with the paragraph and clip 4 (rebuilt) it stays at 29.8%. Unclipped, it keeps only 76% of its first-token probability on AIRisk's answer format, where each of its three passes keeps 99% or more: dividing by p− lifts the tokens neg-align rules out. The choice, made within the format, is not affected. main-v3's teacher reads the scenarios paragraph instead, at clip 4: rebuilt, that q scores 85.5% right and 29.9% risky.

findings.sub: CE only on main-v3, no AFT: % right · % risky
findings.title: On main-v3, KD adds nothing to CE.
findings.body: CE + windowed KD ties CE only (−0.9 points right, p 0.18; −0.2 risky, p 0.69). The fixed anchor costs on both (−3.2 and +5.5): all 85 one-risky dilemmas where it is risky and CE only safe are risky for Instruct too. The KD students do separate the documents (test D− minus D+: 0.77 nats per token windowed, 0.45 CE only), but the scores follow the fit to D+ (1.247 and 1.244, fixed anchor 1.399).

findings.title: The teacher's tilt alone moves AIRisk.
findings.body: With no CE the student moves only toward its tilted snapshot. Risky choices fall 13.0 points from Instruct's 36.6% (168 dilemmas turn safe, 2 risky), against 19.6 for the teacher in context. ConstitutionEval moves +1.2, to the teacher in context's 87.0%. On the one-risky dilemmas it is safer than q itself (20.9% risky against 27.4%): it turns 85 of the 88 dilemmas q makes safe, and 168 in all. The clip limits q on each eval item, not what the student learns from the documents.

findings.sub: windowed − CE only, item by item, against q's tilt (ConstitutionEval, partial)
findings.title: KD moves the eval probabilities toward the teacher, not the answers.
findings.body: The KD students answer more sharply than CE only: the right answer's median margin is 58.8 nats for CE only, 72.9 windowed and 76.9 with the fixed anchor (Instruct 82.2, q 100.2). Beyond that scale, each item's difference follows q's tilt on it: partial correlation 0.40 windowed and 0.65 fixed anchor against CE only, 0.78 KD only against Instruct. But the tilt points away from the right answer on 29 of CE only's 45 misses, and windowed pushes those further, by −11.1 nats on average.

findings.sub: % right: CE only vs its teacher in context
findings.title: CE only already beats its teacher in context.
findings.body: On both benchmarks: 93.4% against 87.0% right, 11.2% against 17.0% risky. On CE only's 45 ConstitutionEval misses, the teacher in context is right on 14 and q on 17. Of its 100 risky choices on the one-risky dilemmas, the teacher in context makes 77 too and q 85. Copying this teacher cannot add much over CE on these benchmarks, whatever the anchor.

questions.q: Can the evals see a spec in context?
questions.answer: Yes, in the right direction: SPP +2.7 points right and −9.7 risky, pro-align +2.5 and −17.1. On ConstitutionEval the effect is small next to training.

questions.q: Does a spec's mirror read as worse?
questions.answer: neg-align does in every form (−9.6, +38.3; with the scenarios paragraph −41.0, +54.3). neg-SPP only with the scenarios paragraph (−65.6, +51.8); read alone or with the values paragraph it scores as better (+4.1, −6.8). SPP's mirror was dropped from main-v3 before the scenarios runs.

questions.q: Is it Qwen's safety tuning that refuses neg-SPP?
questions.answer: No. The pretrained model scores neg-SPP + paragraph at 91.0%, against 90.1% for SPP.

questions.q: What does ConstitutionEval measure with a spec in context?
questions.answer: While the spec is only read, principled against compromise: either sign drops the subtle wrong option, and SPP minus neg-SPP is −1.5 points. Told to decide by the spec (the scenarios paragraph), which spec: SPP minus neg-SPP is +70.2.

questions.q: Where does the KD target land?
questions.answer: At Instruct on ConstitutionEval (85.8%), between Instruct and pro-align on AIRisk (30.1%), held back by the clip there. With both specs + values paragraph and no clip it stays at Instruct on ConstitutionEval (86.4%) and goes below pro-align + paragraph in context on AIRisk (16.7% risky). main-v3's teacher (scenarios paragraph, clip 4), rebuilt: 85.5% and 29.9% risky.

questions.q: Does KD add to CE on main-v3?
questions.answer: No. Windowed KD ties CE only (−0.9 right, −0.2 risky); the fixed anchor costs (−3.2, +5.5). One seed each, no AFT.

questions.q: Does KD change the eval probabilities?
questions.answer: Yes, but not the picks. The KD students stay sharper than CE only, and each item moves along q's tilt (partial r 0.40 on ConstitutionEval, 0.11 on AIRisk, windowed against CE only). The tilt is wrong on most of CE only's misses.

questions.q: What does the tilt do alone?
questions.answer: Windowed KD only: −13.0 points risky and +1.2 right against Instruct, at the teacher in context on ConstitutionEval.

students.lead: Four students of Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct, each a fresh LoRA trained for 384 steps on main-v3's 3,066 pairs of pro-align (D+) and neg-align (D−) documents, seed 42, scored with no AFT and no spec in context. The teacher reads each spec followed by the scenarios paragraph; its target q tilts the anchor by α 1 · clip₄(log p+ − log p−). CE only scores best on both benchmarks, and KD adds no points to it.
students.docs: Test D+ and D−: the student's NLL in nats per token on main-v3's 160 test pairs (Instruct: step 0), from the training run's own diagnostics. KD separates the documents more than CE alone (D− − D+ 0.77 windowed, 0.81 fixed anchor, 0.45 CE only), but the scores follow D+: windowed and CE only share it, the fixed anchor's is worse.
students.probs: The same students' probabilities on the eval items, from the saved rows. ConstitutionEval: the right answer's margin over the best wrong option (summed over the four rotations, nats) and its probability among the four letters. AIRisk: the risky action's log-odds over the safe one (both label orders summed), on the 1,237 dilemmas with exactly one risky action. q is rebuilt from the teacher's two passes at α 1 and clip 4.
students.partial: Each item's difference a − b against q's tilt on it (q minus Instruct), after both are fitted on b's own metric and Instruct's: a uniform sharpening or flattening is not counted. CE only against Instruct is shown for scale: on AIRisk the pro-align documents alone move along the tilt, which there mostly means the safe action.
students.strata: Mean difference a − b in nats, split by whether b gets the item right (ConstitutionEval: the right answer; AIRisk: the safe action) and whether q's tilt points toward the right (or safe) answer or away from it. KD follows the tilt both ways: it pushes b's misses further wrong where the tilt points away.
why: The tilt is wrong where CE only is wrong. It points away from the right answer on 29 of CE only's 45 ConstitutionEval misses and toward it on 11. Of the 10 items CE only gets right and windowed misses, the tilt points away on 7; windowed alone is right on 4.

Where the tilt agrees with CE only, KD only sharpens: on the items CE only gets right with the tilt toward the right answer, windowed adds 15.0 nats on average (528 items). On AIRisk it deepens the safe choices (median −10.9 nats) and flips almost none (11 more risky, 14 fewer).
The fixed anchor keeps Instruct's risky choices: of the 85 one-risky dilemmas where it is risky and CE only safe, Instruct is risky on 85 and q on 84.

CE only beats its teacher in context: 93.4% against 87.0% right, 11.2% against 17.0% risky. On CE only's misses the teacher in context is right on 14 of 45; on its 100 risky choices it is risky on 77. So copying it cannot add much over CE on these benchmarks.

analysis.appeal: neg-align makes both wrong options gain, as a mirror should. neg-SPP with the paragraph makes the blatant one gain but not the subtle one, and SPP makes neither gain. Without the paragraph neg-SPP (15% and 15%) is far closer to SPP than to neg-align. With the scenarios paragraph it is neg-align's equal (98% and 83%, against 96% and 79% for neg-align with the same paragraph).

scoring: SPP's own code (epfl-dlab/spp-evals at cf545a0, unmodified): prompts, answer tokens, rotations and metrics. Only the log probabilities are ours (align_distill/eval/logprobs.py), so that adapters, system turns and q can be scored on one loaded model.

ConstitutionEval: each item at its four cyclic rotations; the first-token log probability of each letter ("A" and " A" pooled) is summed per option over its four slots, so the position prior cancels; the highest sum is the answer. dlab-spp/constitution-eval at 0f3de9d (CC-BY-4.0).

AIRisk: both actions in the prompt; log P(" Action 1") against log P(" Action 2") after "Answer:", in both label orders, summed. dlab-spp/airisk_dilemmas at b93c856, audit-confirmed risk labels; the value map from kellycyy/AIRiskDilemmas at 8674d1f.
No sampling, no judge, no API. One forward pass per prompt, first token, no reasoning.
Intervals: the exact 95% bootstrap over items (a resampled count is binomial, a paired difference multinomial). Comparisons: McNemar's exact test on the items where only one model is right, or risky.
setup.framing: A spec goes into the system turn as the teacher reads it in distillation (the spec frame, then the chat template's own system line), before the benchmark's own user turn, which tells the model it has not read any framework document. The values paragraph is a closing paragraph after the spec: follow the constitution (or the Model Spec) above. The scenarios paragraph, main-v3's teacher text, says instead that the model will be given scenarios and should decide them exactly as the Model Spec above says. The pretrained model is asked in Instruct's chat template. The main-v3 students have no spec in context.

limits: One forward pass and the first token: no reasoning, no sampling. SPP's generative path for models of 4B and up was not run.
The benchmark's user turn says the model has not read any framework document and should use its own judgment, which pulls against a spec in the system turn.
ConstitutionEval's bands and hardening come from a small model (gemma-3n-e4b); 252 of the 678 items were hardened against it.
The pretrained model puts only about half of its probability on AIRisk's answer format.
The prompts and the analyses were chosen after reading these results, and about 30 comparisons share the same items without correction.
The main-v3 students have one seed each and no AFT. The paired p values count items, not seeds.
